do_headline: Getting out is only the beginning.
Support that doesn’t stop at the door.
do_body:
Leaving an abusive relationship does not mean the struggle is over.

For many women, it is the beginning of a much longer journey — healing from what they have experienced, rebuilding their confidence, caring for their children, finding stability and learning how to move forward again.

At Strandfold Support Foundation, we believe that healing requires more than simply leaving. It requires a safe space to talk, professional psychological support and someone to walk alongside you as you begin to rebuild.

Our work begins with counselling and emotional support. Where we are able and where resources permit, we also provide practical assistance to help address some of the challenges that may stand in the way of rebuilding.

We may not always be able to provide everything a woman needs. But we believe that every woman deserves to be heard, supported and treated with dignity as she finds her way forward.

**Getting out is not the end of the story. It is the beginning of rebuilding a life.**

Getting out is not the end of the story. It is the beginning of a much longer one — the counselling, the court dates, the paperwork, the children’s school fees, the question of where the next month’s income comes from.

Most support ends after the emergency. Ours is built for what follows.
quote_text: The work you are doing is good. It is a good thing you are doing.
I did not come here to be pitied. I came because I needed a lawyer, a counsellor and a way to feed my children. I got all three, and nobody made me feel small for asking.

band_headline: One strand breaks. Folded, we hold.
band_body:
A single strand is fragile. Pull it and it breaks. But strands folded together — twisted, layered, held — become rope strong enough to carry weight that would snap any one of them alone.

The older sense of **fold** is a shelter: an enclosure where the vulnerable are kept through the night. Not forever. Long enough for morning.

That is the work. Not rescue. Not charity. A place to be held, and enough hands folded together to carry what one woman was never meant to carry by herself.
close_headline: If you are reading this for someone else, you are already helping.
close_body: Send her this page. Or call us yourself and ask what to do — you do not need her permission to ask us how to support her well. We will not contact her without her consent.

hero_headline: You don’t need proof. You don’t need a plan. You just need to start.
hero_lede: You do not have to call it abuse. You do not have to be sure. You do not have to have decided anything. If something in your relationship, your home or your workplace is making you afraid, you can talk to us.
hero_assure: **Everything you tell us is confidential. We will not contact anyone without your permission. There is no cost.**
steps_eyebrow: What happens when you contact us
close_headline: You are not the first. You will not be alone.
close_body: There is no minimum threshold. If you are asking whether it is bad enough to count, you are welcome here.

steps.title: You talk. We listen.
steps.body: Somewhere private, by phone or in person. No interrogation. You share what you want to share, and we ask your permission before we write anything down.

steps.title: We check you are safe now.
steps.body: If you are in danger, we help you make a safety plan and connect you to emergency services. If you or a child needs a doctor, that comes first.

steps.title: You choose what happens next.
steps.body: Counselling with us, and referrals only where you want them: medical care, legal aid, a shelter, the police, or help to earn an income. We do not decide anything for you.

steps.title: We stay.
steps.body: Follow-up sessions and regular check-ins for as long as you want them. You can close your case whenever you choose, and if you come back later, the door is open.

steps.title: You talk. We listen.
steps.body: No interrogation, no forms first. You share what you want to share.

steps.title: We tell you your options.
steps.body: All of them, honestly, including the ones that are difficult.

steps.title: You choose.
steps.body: We do not decide anything for you.

steps.title: We stay.
steps.body: Whatever you choose, we follow up — and if you change your mind later, the door is open.

accordions.title: Is this abuse?
accordions.body:
Abuse is not only physical. If any of these are familiar, you are welcome here:

**Physical** — hitting, choking, restraining, throwing objects, harm to your children or pets.

**Emotional and psychological** — constant criticism, humiliation, threats, silent treatment as punishment, being told you are mad or imagining things.

**Sexual** — any sexual act you did not freely agree to, including within marriage.

**Financial** — controlling your money, preventing you from working, taking your earnings, keeping you in debt.

**Digital** — monitoring your phone, tracking your location, demanding passwords, sharing your images without consent.

**Isolation** — being cut off from family, friends, church, work or medical care.

**Spiritual** — using scripture, faith or a religious leader’s authority to justify control or to force you to stay.

**You do not need to tick every box. One is enough.**

accordions.title: Safety planning
accordions.body:
A safety plan is not a decision to leave. It is a set of options ready in case you need them.

Identify one person outside the home who knows your situation.

Know which room in the house has an exit and no weapons; avoid kitchens and bathrooms during conflict.

Keep a small bag of essentials somewhere safe — with a neighbour, at work, at church.

Photograph and store key documents in a private cloud account he does not know about: ID, birth certificates, marriage certificate, property papers, medical records.

Agree a code word with someone you trust that means “call for help”.

Memorise two phone numbers in case your phone is taken.

If you have children, agree on where they go and who they call.

Our team will work through a full, personalised plan with you. This list is a starting point only.

accordions.title: For friends and family
accordions.body:
**Say:** “I believe you.” · “This is not your fault.” · “I’m here whether you stay or go.”

**Don’t say:** “Why don’t you just leave?” · “Are you sure it was that bad?” · “Think about the children.”

Do not confront the abuser. Do not issue ultimatums. Do not withdraw when she does not do what you want. Isolation is the abuser’s most effective tool — your steady presence is the counterweight.

**Call us.** You can get guidance on supporting her without breaching her trust.

accordions.title: Finding a shelter
accordions.body:
We do not publish shelter addresses. Publishing them puts every woman inside at risk.

What we do instead: we refer you to a partner facility we have inspected ourselves, we confirm there is space before you travel, and we arrange transport where we can.

To start that process, call or message the helpline. You do not need a referral from anyone.

accordions.title: What this costs you
accordions.body:
Nothing. Counselling, safety planning, referrals and programme access are free. Donors cover the cost.

Nobody at Strandfold will ever ask you for money, gifts or favours, and nobody will ask you to tell your story publicly in exchange for help. If anyone claiming to represent us does, that is not us — please [tell us](/policies#complaints).

hero_headline: Safety is not the finish line.
hero_lede: A woman who is safe but has no income, no counsel and no legal standing has been moved from one kind of trap to another. Our programmes are built as a continuum — most women move through several, at their own pace, over months or years.

approach.title: Trauma-informed, always
approach.body:
Our team is trained to recognise that trauma changes how a person remembers, speaks, trusts and decides. A survivor who tells her story out of order is not lying. A survivor who returns to her abuser has not failed.

We build our processes around how trauma actually behaves, not around how we wish it behaved.

approach.title: Survivor-led, not survivor-managed
approach.body: Women who have come through our programmes sit on our advisory board and shape our services. The people closest to the problem are closest to the solution.

approach.title: We do not pressure anyone to leave
approach.body:
This is the hardest thing to explain to donors and the most important thing we do. On average, a woman attempts to leave an abusive relationship several times before it holds.

Each attempt is information, not failure. A woman who knows we will still be here when she returns is a woman who eventually comes back for the last time.

approach.title: Confidentiality you can rely on
approach.body:
We do not share names, case files, photographs or identifying details with anyone — media, donors, family, employers — without explicit written consent, which can be withdrawn at any moment.

The only exceptions are where the law requires it or someone is at serious risk of harm, and we explain that at the start rather than after the fact.

values.title: She Leads
values.body: The survivor decides. We do not decide for her, pressure her to leave, or withdraw support if she returns. We provide options, information and honesty, and we respect the choice she makes with them.

values.title: Confidentiality Is Sacred
values.body: What is shared with us stays with us. No names, no photographs, no case details without explicit, written, revocable consent.

values.title: Dignity Over Pity
values.body: We do not trade in tragedy for donations. No shock imagery. No woman is asked to perform her worst day to be worth helping.

values.title: Practical Over Performative
values.body: Awareness campaigns do not pay rent. Every programme must produce a measurable change in a woman’s safety, health, legal standing or income.

values.title: The Long Walk
values.body: Recovery is not an event. We measure success in years, not rescues.

hero_lede: These are not case studies. They are accounts of what women built, in their own words, on their own terms.
consent_note:
**Every story on this page is shared with the written, informed consent of the woman it belongs to.** Names, locations and identifying details have been changed.

Consent can be withdrawn at any time, and any story will be removed within 24 hours of that request.

No photograph on this page depicts a Strandfold participant unless she has specifically asked to be photographed.

stories.headline: Abosede … Finding Her Feet Again
stories.body:
Abosede came to Strandfold Support Foundation after experiencing domestic abuse and being left to care for her children without the support she needed.

At Strandfold, she received counselling and emotional support as she began to process what she had experienced and regain her footing.

We also supported her with accommodation, healthcare and financial assistance to start a small business, giving her an opportunity to begin rebuilding her livelihood.

**Her message to us was simple:**

**“Thanks ma. I really appreciate. You help me greatly. God will continue to bless you ma.”**

Her story is not only about what happened to her. It is about what became possible when she received support to begin again.

stories.headline: Ada … An Opportunity to Start Again
stories.body:
Ada came to Strandfold Support Foundation after experiencing domestic violence.

Alongside psychological counselling we provided financial assistance to help her start a small business.

With that support, Ada began putting her business together and taking steps towards becoming financially independent.

**She expressed her gratitude in her own words:**

**“My appreciation also goes to the organisation, Strandfold Support Foundation. May God Almighty be with you, and may the organisation move higher in Jesus’ name. I really appreciate.”**

She also told us:

**“The work you are doing is good. It is a good thing you are doing.”**

stories.headline: A Mother and Her Children … Finding Safety and Care
stories.body:
She came to us after experiencing abuse and being abandoned by her spouse, leaving her to care for her children in extremely difficult circumstances.

At a time when the family needed both emotional and practical support, Strandfold provided emotional support, together with medical care and accommodation.

The intervention gave the family a safer place to stay while addressing their immediate healthcare needs.

hero_headline: The questions people ask before they call.
hero_lede: If yours is not here, ask us. You do not have to give your name to ask a question.

faqs.q: Is it really free?
faqs.a: Yes. Counselling, safety planning, referrals and programme access cost you nothing. Donors cover it.

faqs.q: Will you tell my husband, my family or my employer?
faqs.a: No. Nothing that identifies you is shared without your consent. The only exceptions are where the law requires it, or where you, a child or someone else is at serious risk of harm — and where it is safe to, we will tell you first.

faqs.q: What do you write down about me?
faqs.a:
Only what we need to support you, and only after you agree. Your file is kept locked or password-protected, only the staff working with you can see it, and it is securely destroyed once it is no longer needed.

When we report to the people who fund us, we use numbers and anonymised summaries — never your name. [Read our confidentiality policy](/policies#confidentiality).

faqs.q: Can I stop at any time?
faqs.a: Yes. Using our services is voluntary. You can withdraw whenever you want, and your case can be closed at your request. If you come back later, we will be here.

faqs.q: Do I have to report to the police?
faqs.a: No. Many women choose not to, and that is your decision. We will explain what reporting involves so you can decide with full information, and we will support you either way.

faqs.q: Do I have to leave my husband?
faqs.a: No. We do not pressure anyone to leave. Many women come to us while still in the relationship, and we help them stay as safe as possible.

faqs.q: What if I go back to him?
faqs.a: Then we are still here. This is normal and it is not a failure. Come back whenever you are ready.

faqs.q: I’m not sure it’s bad enough to count.
faqs.a: If you are asking that question, you are welcome here. There is no minimum threshold.

faqs.q: Do you help men?
faqs.a: Our programmes are designed for women and children, which is where our clinical expertise and safeguarding structures lie. Men experiencing abuse can contact us and we will refer you to organisations equipped to help.

faqs.q: Can I volunteer if I’m a survivor myself?
faqs.a: Yes, and many of our team are. We ask that you be at a stable point in your own recovery, and we will discuss this openly and supportively during screening.

faqs.q: Where do you operate?
faqs.a: We are based in Lagos and work with women and children across Lagos State. If you are outside Lagos, contact us anyway and we will help you find support near you.

faqs.q: How do I make a complaint about Strandfold or someone who works here?
faqs.a: You can report anything that worries you — including about a staff member or volunteer — and you do not have to give your name. We acknowledge every report within 5 working days, and nobody who raises a concern in good faith will be penalised for it. [How to raise a concern](/policies#complaints).

faqs.q: Can someone see that I visited this website?
faqs.a:
Possibly. A browser keeps a history of the pages you open, and a shared account or a monitored phone can show more than that.

Use the red **Quick exit** button at the top of any page to leave this site immediately, and open the “Cover your tracks” link for step-by-step instructions.

hero_headline: The rules we hold ourselves to.
hero_lede: Everyone who works with Strandfold — staff, volunteers, consultants, interns, board members and partner representatives — agrees to these policies. These are plain-language summaries. Ask us if you would like the full documents.

policies.title: Safeguarding and child protection
policies.body:
Strandfold is committed to a safe environment for every woman and child who uses our services. **We have zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, neglect, harassment or any other harm.** A child is anyone under 18.

**What we commit to:** safe recruitment and background screening for everyone who works with us; safeguarding orientation for all personnel; strict confidentiality of survivor information; a prompt response to every concern; and compliance with Nigerian and Lagos State protection laws.

**What everyone representing us must do:** treat the people we support with dignity and respect, keep professional boundaries, and avoid any inappropriate physical or emotional relationship. **Nobody acting for Strandfold may ever ask you for gifts, money or favours.**

**Raising a concern:** contact us by phone, WhatsApp or email and ask for our Safeguarding Officer. Every report is documented and investigated confidentially. A breach of this policy can lead to suspension, dismissal or referral to the police.

policies.title: Confidentiality and data protection
policies.body:
**We collect only the information we need to support you, and only with your informed consent.**

What you tell us is used to provide your support. When we report to the people who fund our work, we use numbers and anonymised summaries — never anything that identifies you.

**When we may have to share information without consent:** where the law requires it, or where you, a child or someone else is at serious risk of harm. Where it is safe to, we will tell you first.

**How records are kept:** paper files in locked cabinets, digital records protected by passwords, and access limited to the staff working with you.

**How long we keep them:** only as long as the law and our work require. Then they are securely destroyed.

**If something goes wrong:** any data breach is reported immediately to our Executive Director and put right promptly.

policies.title: This website and your privacy
policies.body:
This website sets no cookies, runs no analytics or advertising, and loads nothing from any other company’s servers, so no advertising or analytics company learns that you visited.

Like every website, our hosting server keeps a short technical log of requests. It is not used to identify visitors.

If you send us a message through the contact form, we see only what you type into it, and we do not send an automatic reply.

**Your own device can still show that you were here** — your browser history, a shared account or a monitored phone. The cover-your-tracks guide, linked at the bottom of every page, explains how to clear it.

policies.title: Sexual harassment
policies.body:
Sexual harassment is prohibited in any form, in our workplace and in our programmes.

It includes unwelcome advances, inappropriate touching, sexual comments, coercion, and any behaviour that creates a hostile environment.

Complaints can be made confidentially to a designated officer and are investigated fairly and promptly. **Retaliation against anyone who complains is prohibited.** Confirmed violations can lead to dismissal and legal action.

policies.title: Code of conduct
policies.body:
Everyone who represents Strandfold, online and offline, must act with integrity and professionalism, treat everyone without discrimination, keep confidential information confidential, avoid conflicts of interest, and use the Foundation’s resources responsibly.

**If anyone claiming to act for Strandfold asks you for money, gifts or favours in return for help, that is not us.** Please report it using the steps below.

policies.title: Complaints and whistleblowing
policies.body:
You can report misconduct, fraud, abuse of power, a safeguarding breach or any unethical behaviour by anyone connected with Strandfold. That includes if you are someone we support.

**How to report:** email our Executive Director at [Executive Director’s email], or write to the Chair of our Board of Trustees at [Board Chair’s address]. **You do not have to give your name.** Anonymous reports are accepted.

**What happens next:** we acknowledge your report within 5 working days, carry out a preliminary review, open a formal investigation where needed, record what we find, and put corrective measures in place.

**Anyone who raises a concern in good faith is protected from retaliation.**

_desc: How Strandfold Support Foundation safeguards women and children, protects personal information, and handles complaints and whistleblowing.
